target_customer: Hardware and engineering teams that order custom mechanical parts from CAD files
problem: Ordering CNC machined parts still runs through phone calls and PDFs across thousands of shops, making quotes and delivery slow and costly.
business_model: Manufacturing service: AI quoting and production planning, revenue per part ordered
product_category: AI enabled on demand manufacturing for mechanical parts

founders.name: Prerit Oberai
founders.background_notes: Listed as cofounder and CTO by third party profiles

competitors.name: Xometry
competitors.what: Marketplace with instant algorithmic quoting across CNC, 3D printing, sheet metal and molding

competitors.name: Fictiv
competitors.what: Instant quoting and automated design for manufacturability review for CNC

competitors.name: Protolabs Network (Hubs)
competitors.what: Own factories plus a network of 250+ partners for prototypes

competitors.name: Plethora
competitors.what: CNC machining with strong design feedback

technical_complexity.rationale: Turning CAD into manufacturable plans with automated design review and quality control requires geometry processing and a shop network, hard for two people.

defensibility.rationale: Large funded platforms already offered instant quoting and design review, so the AI wrapper was easy for rivals to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not known. Incumbents were shipping AI quoting features in 2025 to 2026; no source describes an acquirer.

market_need_then: Competitor marketing and the company's own launch page describe thousands of local and offshore shops still quoting by phone and PDF, and tariff driven interest in domestic sourcing; no independent demand data was retrieved.

branding.domain_note: prototyping.io, a .io domain; no purchase history found

identity.logo: SVG wordmark, not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and technical: 'Turn CAD designs into CNC Machined parts - driven by AI'

brand_strength.rationale: The name is a generic description shared with prototyping software tools and no press on the brand exists, so it is hard to search for and not memorable.

outcome_analysis: Prototyping.io joined YC in Spring 2026 with a CAD to CNC part pitch and was reported to have raised a seed of $6.2M, with one outlet saying it paused hiring after plans changed. YC lists it as Acquired, but no buyer, date or press coverage of a deal was found, and its own site still takes early access sign ups. The outcome is therefore unverified.
notes: Status Acquired is from the YC directory only; two searches found no acquirer or deal coverage, so exit has no date or acquirer. Seed figures conflict: $6.2M (American Bazaar), $4.01M (Dealroom), $130k and $500k pre seed (aggregators); none has named investors, and the $6.2M and $4.01M figures are single outlet claims, so no round is recorded as verified. Founder list differs by source (YC page names only Bodepudi in one fetch, search results name Oberai as CTO). Competitors shown are incumbents named in 2025 to 2026 coverage, near the batch date. Update: the 6.2M seed (raised June 2026 from unnamed venture firms and angels) is recorded from American Bazaar and Dealroom News, which both repeat the founder's LinkedIn post, so it rests on a single self-report. Dealroom's profile lists 4.01M and aggregators 130K and 500K; these conflict and are not summed.
